encodingDesc.p: Printed small capitals transcribed in uppercase; ordinary line-wrap hyphenation joined explicitly; lexical hyphens, spelling, punctuation, brackets and printed footnote pointers retained. Raw digital HTML/XML, scan crops and source bytes remain recoverable. Comparisons may fold case and ae/æ; original source readings are retained without such folding.

normalization.p: Sentence-case presentation is an editorial layer, not a replacement transcription. Each choice retains the exact accepted 1856 text in orig and a case-only display in reg. Proper names, ligatures, punctuation, spelling, source pointers and Roman labels are preserved; common nouns are lowercased. Compiled-index CSS selects reg only, without altering other witnesses.

revisionDesc.change: Authorized human browser-review correction: one provenance note immediately below the index title; reversible sentence-case readings and left-aligned presentation. Original 1856 readings and existing structural identities remain intact.

div.head: Whiston’s chapter headings (compiled index)
div.note: Compiled from the chapter headings printed in the Auburn and Rochester edition of Whiston's translation (Alden & Beardsley, 1856). The arrangement as an index is editorial, not an original printed table of contents.

choice.orig: CONTAINING THE INTERVAL OF TWENTY-TWO YEARS.
choice.reg: Containing the interval of twenty-two years.

choice.orig: FROM FADUS THE PROCURATOR TO FLORUS.
choice.reg: From Fadus the procurator to Florus.

choice.orig: A SEDITION OF THE PHILADELPHIANS AGAINST THE JEWS; AND ALSO CONCERNING THE VESTMENTS OF THE HIGH-PRIEST.
choice.reg: A sedition of the Philadelphians against the Jews; and also concerning the vestments of the high-priest.

choice.orig: HOW HELENA, THE QUEEN OF ADIABENE, AND HER SON, IZATES, EMBRACED THE JEWISH RELIGION; AND HOW HELENA SUPPLIED THE POOR WITH CORN, WHEN THERE WAS A GREAT FAMINE AT JERUSALEM.
choice.reg: How Helena, the queen of Adiabene, and her son, Izates, embraced the Jewish religion; and how Helena supplied the poor with corn, when there was a great famine at Jerusalem.

choice.orig: HOW ARTABANUS, THE KING OF PARTHIA, OUT OF FEAR OF THE SECRET CONTRIVANCES OF HIS SUBJECTS AGAINST HIM, WENT TO IZATES, AND WAS BY HIM REINSTATED IN HIS GOVERNMENT; AS ALSO HOW BARDANES, HIS SON, DENOUNCED WAR AGAINST IZATES.
choice.reg: How Artabanus, the king of Parthia, out of fear of the secret contrivances of his subjects against him, went to Izates, and was by him reinstated in his government; as also how Bardanes, his son, denounced war against Izates.

choice.orig: HOW IZATES WAS BETRAYED BY HIS OWN SUBJECTS, AND FOUGHT AGAINST BY THE ARABIANS; AND HOW IZATES, BY THE PROVIDENCE OF GOD, WAS DELIVERED OUT OF THEIR HANDS.
choice.reg: How Izates was betrayed by his own subjects, and fought against by the Arabians; and how Izates, by the providence of God, was delivered out of their hands.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THEUDAS AND THE SONS OF JUDAS THE GALILEAN; AS ALSO WHAT CALAMITY FELL UPON THE JEWS ON THE DAY OF THE PASSOVER.
choice.reg: Concerning Theudas and the sons of Judas the Galilean; as also what calamity fell upon the Jews on the day of the Passover.

choice.orig: HOW THERE HAPPENED A QUARREL BETWEEN THE JEWS AND THE SAMARITANS; AND HOW CLAUDIUS PUT AN END TO THEIR DIFFERENCES.
choice.reg: How there happened a quarrel between the Jews and the Samaritans; and how Claudius put an end to their differences.

choice.orig: FELIX IS MADE PROCURATOR OF JUDEA; AS ALSO CONCERNING AGRIPPA, JUNIOR, AND HIS SISTERS.
choice.reg: Felix is made procurator of Judea; as also concerning Agrippa, junior, and his sisters.

choice.orig: AFTER WHAT MANNER, UPON THE DEATH OF CLAUDIUS, NERO SUCCEEDED IN THE GOVERNMENT; AS ALSO WHAT BARBAROUS THINGS HE DID. CONCERNING THE ROBBERS, MURDERERS, AND IMPOSTORS, THAT AROSE WHILE FELIX AND FESTUS WERE PROCURATORS OF JUDEA.
choice.reg: After what manner, upon the death of Claudius, Nero succeeded in the government; as also what barbarous things he did. Concerning the robbers, murderers, and impostors, that arose while Felix and Festus were procurators of Judea.

choice.orig: CONCERNING ALBINUS, UNDER WHOSE PROCURATORSHIP THE JEWS WERE AGAIN AFFLICTED; AS ALSO WHAT EDIFICES WERE BUILT BY AGRIPPA.
choice.reg: Concerning Albinus, under whose procuratorship the Jews were again afflicted; as also what edifices were built by Agrippa.

choice.orig: CONCERNING FLORUS THE PROCURATOR, WHO NECESSITATED THE JEWS TO TAKE UP ARMS AGAINST THE ROMANS. THE CONCLUSION.
choice.reg: Concerning Florus the procurator, who necessitated the Jews to take up arms against the Romans. The conclusion.
